# Performance budgets — `bracket-filled.fsm`, 1080p viewport

**Generated by** `web/tests/probe-budgets.mjs --out docs/verification/budgets-laptop-chrome.md`, run `2026-10-15`.

The referee is the headed pass (GOAL.md names a real browser on a real display).
The headless pass records what CI sees; headless Chromium holds the main thread on
presented-frame back-pressure inside its GPU-process pipeline for ~100-250 ms after
an edit even though the app JS costs ~0.5 ms per frame — see the note below.

- headless: wasm threaded (cross-origin isolated, pool of 4)
- headless: setup solve 14127 ms; console errors 0

Headless caveat, measured on the referee workstation (SwiftShader and ANGLE/Vulkan
on an RTX 5090): headless Chromium reports one 123-236 ms long task per edit; a trace ties it to a
single GPU-process `WebGL` command-buffer flush of 127-183 ms, with the renderer
main thread waiting inside one umbrella rAF task. Hiding the raymarch quad, hiding
overlays, forced GC and warm shader caches make no difference; the app JS costs
0.2-0.6 ms per frame. The headed run on the same machine records no long tasks and
a 59.9-60.0 fps presented cadence. The headless number is therefore a harness
artifact, and the headed pass is the budget referee.

Export budget (3MF of the graded bracket at 0.1 mm feature resolution, ≤ 15 s): the
"export 3MF at h 0.1" row measures it through the real Make UI in Chrome — mesh time
from the export meta, write time from the timed download click. The click→meta wall
also carries the export health report (field-volume reference and defect scan), which
the budget row does not include; both wall and report times are in the detail.
This run: the row FAILS in headless.
Defect classes and their classification: `docs/verification/V8.md`, section
"Adaptive dual contouring (the browser export path)".

Mesh-doc rows (M6): "mesh doc import" times the shipped 12-triangle GLB fixture
through the real file palette — chooser settle, weld, segment and the worker
voxelise, up to the mesh node landing in the document; "mesh doc export" runs the
same Make-lens 3MF measurement as the bracket row on that imported part. The
fixture is not budget-scale: the 87k-triangle Meshy STL the milestone names is
measured natively in `docs/verification/V10.md`.


Sweep-throughput row (M16, GOAL D4): the V23 cantilever sweep through `fieldsmith api` —
five points on beam.size.2 over 8..12 mm, rungs 30000,150000, tolerance deflection:1%,
in one native process with the costs store off (the table row names the binary's
engine). Points per hour uses the process wall of the whole 5-point ladder, not the
engine sums, so the rate is the honest end-to-end one. The N100 leg of this row is
measured over ssh (the shipped-binary route) and lives in data/costs/costs.csv and
GOAL.md's Performance-budgets ledger, not in this doc.
Machine: Intel(R) N100, 4 hardware threads, 7 GiB RAM, linux. Every timing above is this machine's.

## Appendix: N100 Chrome empirical compute profile (M21)

Measured on `ian-quieter.lan` (`Intel(R) N100`, 4 hardware threads, 7 GiB RAM, headless Linux, no hardware GPU/display).
During v0.4 (M13), headless Chrome on the N100 recorded two wall bands (`4918 / 15064 ms` vs `9679 / 24967 ms` for `edit → coarse` / `edit → refined`).
Isolating the runtime factors in M21 identified two mechanisms:

1. **Software WebGL (`SwiftShader` 1080p) shader inlining and redundant rAF invalidations:**
   - Before M12 (`3d021558`), the outer body shader compiled only `fs_field(p)` (`~750 ms`/frame on 4 N100 cores, `1.8 fps`), and unthrottled UI syncs triggered 7 frames during the solve (`5555 ms` total SwiftShader CPU), yielding `4918 / 15064 ms`.
   - M12 added `if (u_core > 0.5) return fs_core(p); return fs_field(p);` to the shared fragment shader and mounted `setCore` + `updateParamGrid` on every edit/arrival. Even with `u_core = 0` (`bodyAlpha = 1`, opaque body), SwiftShader inlined the gyroid lattice (`fs_core`, `u_param` 3D texture fetches, `3 × fs_sincos`) into the 300-step raymarch loop, raising per-frame CPU cost to `~2100 ms` (`0.9 fps`) across 9 solve-window frames (`18937 ms` total SwiftShader CPU) and stretching the solve to `9679 / 24967 ms`.
   - **M21 fix (`viewport.ts`, `ViewportHost.tsx`, `setup.tsx`, `results.tsx`, `make.tsx`):** specializing `fragSource` per pass (`fs_field` when `core = false`, `fs_core` when `core = true`), deferring `coreMaterial` construction and `u_param` uploads until `bodyAlpha < 1`, holding the render loop while `compileAsync` is in flight, and deduplicating highlight/gizmo/glyph invalidations reduces solve-window renders to the **3 visual updates** (`edit`, `coarse` glyphs, `refined` glyphs; `2365 ms` total SwiftShader CPU) and brings N100 Chrome down to **`3272–3285 / 13351–13409 ms`** (`1.9 fps` at 100 % opacity, `0.8–0.9 fps` at 35 % opacity).
   - Pausing `vp.render` during the edit solve (`paused-webgl-worker-only`) eliminates the single `635 ms` edit-frame overlap before `coarse`, measuring **`2746 / 13288 ms`** (`0` long tasks), matching WebGL-less headless Firefox (`2963 / 12670 ms`) within `7 %`.
2. **Profile cache vs. sustained PL1 package thermal/power clamping:**
   - Cool-start runs (`38 °C` package temperature, all 4 cores at `2.9–3.1 GHz`) reproduce within `0.4 %` (`3272 / 13351 ms`, `3280 / 13363 ms`, `3274 / 13409 ms`, `3285 / 13377 ms`).
   - Back-to-back warm-profile runs after sustained 4-core load (`63 °C` package temperature, PL1 clamping one core to `1.69 GHz`) add `+11.9–13.3 %` (`3722 / 14968 ms`); local loopback `.wasm` streaming compilation (`~80 ms`) is smaller than the PL1 thermal/power step.

| :-- | --: | --: | --: | :-- | :-- |

| Post-M12 / v0.4 (`fs_core` inlined, 9 rAFs) | 23957 | 9679 | 24967 | 9 frames (`18937 ms` sum, `0.9 fps`) | `~38 °C`, `2.9–3.1 GHz` |
